title: Sacramento Sheriffs Office Shoot Of Ingold Guttenbeil

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

A. The October 4, 2026 shooting (Pen. Code § 832.7(b)(1)(A)(i))

This incident involved the discharge of firearms at a person by peace officers, so all records listed in § 832.7(b)(2) are subject to disclosure, including:

All investigative reports, including incident, supplemental, and use-of-force reports.
All photographic, audio, and video evidence, including body-worn camera, dash/in-car camera, surveillance or business video collected from the car wash or neighboring businesses, and any bystander video the Office obtained.
All 911 call audio, dispatch radio audio, and CAD records for the call that prompted the response.
Transcripts or recordings of interviews with deputies, witnesses, and the reporting party.
The autopsy report and any coroner's records in the Office's possession.
All materials compiled and presented to the District Attorney or any other body charged with determining whether to file charges, or whether the deputies' conduct complied with law and policy.
All documents setting forth findings or recommended findings, and any disciplinary records relating to the incident.
The names, badge numbers, and assignments of the three deputies who fired. Officer names are not confidential. (Commission on Peace Officer Standards & Training v. Superior Court (2007) 42 Cal.4th 278.)
Records identifying the firearm the Office reports recovering, its location when found, and any evidence-collection or chain-of-custody records documenting where it was found.

B. Critical incident video (Gov. Code § 7923.625)

Separately from Part A, I request all video and audio recordings of this critical incident. The Office has stated publicly that it intends to release body-worn camera footage. If release is delayed, please state the specific basis for the delay in writing, as the statute requires.

C. Related incidents involving Mr. Guttenbeil (Gov. Code §§ 7923.610, 7923.615)

The Office has publicly linked Mr. Guttenbeil to two prior incidents. I request the information the statute requires to be disclosed for:

The alleged shooting at the Marconi/Eastern intersection on the night of October 3, 2026: time, date, and location; time and date of report; factual circumstances; description of any injuries, property, or weapons involved; and CAD records.
The June 2026 arrest at the same intersection for suspected assault with a deadly weapon: arrestee information, factual circumstances of the arrest, charges, and the disposition.

D. Prior records of the involved deputies (Pen. Code § 832.7(b)(1))

For each of the three deputies who fired, all records of any other incident involving:
the discharge of a firearm at a person;
use of force resulting in death or great bodily injury;
a sustained finding of unreasonable or excessive force;
failure to intervene;
dishonesty;
unlawful arrest or search;
prejudice or discrimination.

E. Policies

The Office's use-of-force policy, de-escalation policy, body-worn camera policy, and critical-incident video release policy in effect on October 4, 2026.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

communications.subject: Louisiana Public Records Law Request: Incident Report Data
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Louisiana Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

For purposes of this request, "officer" means a sworn member of the police of any rank, and "data" means logs, tables, or datasets maintained in a machine-readable format (such as spreadsheets or database exports).
The timeframe for all portions of this request is all responsive records that exist in a machine-readable format from January 1, 2020 through the most recent date data is collected, and that can be produced as a spreadsheet or similar electronic file.
I request data sufficient to show any and all information maintained by the New Orleans Police Department regarding incident and offense reports recorded in NOPD's records management system. This should include all incidents recorded by NOPD regardless of whether the incident resulted in arrest, regardless of clearance status, and regardless of whether the underlying call was generated through 911, non-emergency line, officer-initiated activity, or walk-in/online reporting.
This request is specifically for the full underlying incident record set, including data fields that are not currently included in any publicly-released file on data.nola.gov (including the "Electronic Police Report" datasets) or any other public release. I am aware that subsets of NOPD incident data are published publicly. The publicly-released files omit fields that are necessary for the research purposes of this request, including but not limited to the originating CAD event identifier needed to link incidents to calls for service handled by OPCD, full offense-level detail in multi-offense incidents, victim and offender demographic detail, clearance status with date, and reporting officer assignment. I am requesting all fields below that exist in the underlying record system, regardless of whether they currently appear in any public release. A referral to a publicly-released subset is not responsive to this request.
Please provide the data in CSV, TXT, or XML format (machine-readable; not XLSX). For each incident, please include the following fields where they exist in the system:
Identifiers and CAD Linkage

Item Number (NOPD)
Originating CAD Event Number (the field needed to link this incident to the corresponding CAD record in OPCD calls-for-service data)
Case Number (if distinct from item number)
Linked Arrest Identifier(s), if any arrests resulted from the incident

Incident Timestamps

Date and Time of Incident (occurrence start)
Date and Time of Incident End (if range recorded)
Date and Time Reported to NOPD
Date and Time of Clearance (if cleared)

Incident Location

Address (block-level / hundred-block) or intersection
Latitude / Longitude
NOPD District (1st through 8th)
Zone or subdistrict
Council District
Census Tract (please indicate whether 2010 or 2020 vintage; both preferred)
ZIP code
Premise Type / Location Code

Offense Information (one record per offense)

Offense Sequence Number within the incident
Offense Code (NOPD signal code, NIBRS code if available, and Louisiana Revised Statutes / NOLA Municipal Code section)
Offense Description
Offense Class or Degree (felony, misdemeanor, municipal ordinance violation)
Attempted vs. Completed indicator
Weapon / Force Used
Bias Motivation / Hate Crime indicator
Domestic Violence indicator
Drug-Involved indicator

Victim Information (one record per victim, where applicable)

Victim Sequence Number
Victim Type
Age (or Year of Birth)
Sex
Race
Ethnicity (if stored separately from race)
Injury Type(s)
Relationship of Victim to Offender(s)

Offender / Suspect Information (one record per offender, where applicable)

Offender Sequence Number
Age (or Year of Birth)
Sex
Race
Ethnicity (if stored separately)
Whether the offender was identified or unknown at time of report

Clearance and Disposition

Disposition Code (NOPD uses dispositions including RTF for report to follow, NAT for necessary action taken, GOA for gone on arrival, UNF for unfounded, and others)
Clearance Status
Date of Clearance
Whether the incident is currently classified as Founded or Unfounded

Property Information (one record per property element, where applicable)

Property Sequence Number
Property Loss Type
Property Description
Property Value

Reporting Officer Information

Reporting Officer First Name
Reporting Officer Middle Name or Initial
Reporting Officer Last Name
Reporting Officer Badge Number or Item Number
Reporting Officer Rank or Title
Reporting Officer Employee ID (if tracked separately from badge number)
Reporting Officer Unit or Assignment at the time of report (district, platoon, or specialized unit)

Optional, if maintained in the system

Reporting Officer Race or Ethnicity
Reporting Officer Gender

If any of the above fields are stored under different names, codes, or tables, I request the functional equivalent fields. If incident data is stored across multiple linked tables, I would prefer to receive each table with its native keys preserved so the relationships can be reconstructed, including the link from the incident record to the originating CAD event.
Please also provide a codebook or data dictionary so that the data provided can be appropriately understood, including the NOPD signal code list, the disposition code list, and any internal clearance code definitions used in the export. If a Zoom call or meeting is preferred to a codebook, that is fine.
If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific exemption you feel justifies the refusal to release the information and notify me of the appeal procedures available to me under the law. To the extent any individual field above is exempt under La. R.S. 44:3 or any other exception, please redact only that field and produce the remainder.
Please confirm receipt of this request within three business days as required by La. R.S. 44:32 / 44:33, and provide a tracking number. I am happy to discuss scoping, format, or staged production by year if that would expedite response.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Filed Requests

- Freecash.com
- Free Cash app
- FreeSkins / freeskins.com
- Almedia GmbH
- Almedia USA, Inc.
- Almedia Ops UK Ltd

Include complaints contributed by other organizations (such as the Better Business Bureau and state attorneys general) to the extent the FTC can release them. Include Do Not Call and unwanted text-message complaints.

I prefer the records as a spreadsheet (CSV or Excel) of complaint fields and narrative text.

Disclosure will add significantly to public understanding of how these practices affect consumers. I have no commercial interest in the records.

Sincerely,

Yax Falk

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Rubinstein trip
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

•	Records concerning the travel of the Legal Adviser of the Department of State (Reed D. Rubinstein) to Israel that was planned for November 2025, including: whether the travel occurred, was postponed, or was cancelled; the dates of travel; the itinerary; the delegation list; and any record of the purpose of the travel.
•	Agendas, schedules, briefing materials, talking points, background papers, and readouts prepared for or generated by that travel, including any materials concerning meetings with Israeli research institutions, non-governmental organizations, or the think-tank community.
•	Records concerning any proposed or actual meeting, during that travel, with the Institute for National Security Studies (INSS) or its personnel, including but not limited to Pnina Sharvit Baruch, Raz Zimmt, and Sima Shine. This includes any correspondence proposing that individuals be included in the delegation or in meetings with the think-tank community.
•	Travel authorizations, travel vouchers, and reimbursement records for the Legal Adviser and any accompanying Department personnel for travel to Israel in the period October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025.
•	Correspondence between the Office of the Legal Adviser and U.S. Embassy Jerusalem (including its Tel Aviv Branch Office), the Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs, or the Executive Secretariat concerning the planning of this travel, from September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025.
•	Any record of contact during 2025 between the Office of the Legal Adviser and the Institute for National Security Studies, including correspondence with the individuals named above.

I ask to be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

•	Records identifying the Political Officer or officers responsible for monitoring, analyzing, or reporting on Iranian affairs at U.S. Embassy Jerusalem and its Tel Aviv Branch Office — including the position designated “Iran Watcher,” held by Andrew H. Doehler until June 2025 — from June 1, 2025 to the date of this request. Specifically: whether that position was filled, abolished, or reassigned; any position description or position number for it; and the name(s) and title(s) of any officer who assumed its duties, including but not limited to J. Claiborne Gayden and Issa Boursheh. This request seeks records of official duties and does not seek personnel, medical, or performance-evaluation records.
•	Calendar entries, daily schedules, meeting invitations, and attendance lists for the officer or officers described above from June 1, 2025 to the date of this request, including but not limited to entries referencing the Institute for National Security Studies, Raz Zimmt, Sima Shine, Pnina Sharvit Baruch, Carmit Valensi, and Eldad Shavit.
•	Email, including attachments thereto, and printed correspondence between employees of U.S. Embassy Jerusalem and its Tel Aviv Branch Office and employees of the Institute for National Security Studies at inss.org.il, from June 1, 2025 to the date of this request. Please include the accounts of Political Officer J. Claiborne Gayden (GaydenJC@state.gov) and Political Specialist Issa Boursheh (BourshehIX@state.gov).
•	Records concerning any outreach initiative, “listening tour,” or series of consultations by U.S. Embassy Jerusalem with Israeli officials, think tanks, and non-governmental organizations regarding the building of formal networks of countries in Africa and Latin America in support of Israel in international organizations, from June 1, 2025 to the date of this request, including terms of reference, target lists, contact logs, briefing materials, and readouts.
•	Meeting memoranda, contact reports, trip reports, readouts, briefing papers, and cables documenting or referring to meetings between Department personnel and employees of the Institute for National Security Studies from June 1, 2025 to the date of this request, including any record of the visit to Israel by a Deputy Assistant Secretary named Donica.
•	Records concerning the Near Eastern Affairs Area Studies Program’s engagement with the Institute for National Security Studies from June 1, 2025 to the date of this request, including invitations, speaker agreements, honoraria, course materials, and correspondence with Raz Zimmt, and the records of program staff Marcus B. Hallinan (HallinanMB@state.gov), Dana M. Helfenbein (HelfenbeinDM@state.gov), and Catherine Batruni (BatruniC@state.gov). This includes any record discussing the application of the Chatham House Rule or the non-recording of these sessions.

INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING SEARCH:
1.	Instructions Regarding “Leads”: As required by the relevant case law, the Department should follow any leads it discovers during the conduct of its searches and perform additional searches when said leads indicate that records may be located in another system. Failure to follow clear leads is a violation of FOIA.
2.	Request for Public Records: Please search for any records even if they are already publicly available.
3.	Request for Duplicate Pages: I request disclosure of any and all supposedly “duplicate” pages. Scholars analyze records not only for the information available on any given page, but also for the relationships between that information and information on pages surrounding it. As such, though certain pages may have been previously released to me, the existence of those pages within new context renders them functionally new pages. Therefore, I request disclosure of all “duplicate” pages.
4.	Request for Search of Records Transferred to Other Agencies: I request that in conducting its search, the Department should disclose releasable records even if they are available publicly through other sources outside the Department. If the Department is unable to do so, it should disclose where specifically the relevant records are available.
5.	Regarding Destroyed Records: If any records responsive or potentially responsive to my request have been destroyed, my request includes, but is not limited to, any and all records relating or referring to the destruction of those records, including any and all records relating or referring to the events leading to the destruction of those records.
6.	Records Systems to Search: Please search all systems likely to contain responsive records, including the records of U.S. Embassy Jerusalem (Political Section) and its Tel Aviv Branch Office; the Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs, including the Office of Iranian Affairs and the Office of Israel and Palestinian Affairs; the Bureau of Intelligence and Research; and the Executive Secretariat’s cable and correspondence records. Please search both classified and unclassified systems, and refer or coordinate with any component, post, or successor office that assumed custody of these records.

INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING SCOPE AND BREADTH OF REQUESTS
Please interpret the scope of this request broadly. The Department is instructed to interpret the scope of this request in the most liberal manner possible short of an interpretation that would lead to a conclusion that the request does not reasonably describe the records sought.

EXEMPTIONS AND SEGREGABILITY
The FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 codified a foreseeable-harm standard at 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A). An agency may withhold information only if it (i) reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption, or (ii) disclosure is prohibited by law. Embarrassment to officials, the possibility that disclosure might reveal errors or failures, and speculative or abstract fears are not legitimate grounds for withholding.
Even where an exemption properly applies to part of a record, the statute requires the agency to release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. If documents are denied in part or in whole, please specify which exemption(s) is (are) claimed for each passage or whole document denied.
Please provide a complete itemized inventory and a detailed factual justification of total or partial denial of documents. Specify the number of pages in each document and the total number of pages pertaining to this request. For “classified” material denied, please include the following information: the classification (confidential, secret or top secret); identity of the classifier; date or event for automatic declassification or classification review or downgrading; if applicable, identity of official authorizing extension of automatic declassification or review past six years; and, if applicable, the reason for extended classification beyond six years.
In excising material, please “black out” the material rather than “white out” or “cut out.” I expect, as provided by FOIA, that the remaining non-exempt portions of documents will be released.
Please release all pages regardless of the extent of excising, even if all that remains are the letterhead, page numbers, or administrative markings.
The names and official titles of federal employees acting in their official capacity, and the organizational placement of government positions, are not personal information protected by Exemption 6 or Exemption 7(C). Please do not withhold such information on personal-privacy grounds.
In addition, I ask that your agency exercise its discretion to release records which may be technically exempt, but where withholding serves no important public interest.

Format requested and fees:
I request that you provide records as they become available, rather than all at once.
Please produce all records with administrative markings and pagination included.
Please send a memo (copy to me) to the appropriate units in your office to assure that no records related to this request are destroyed. Please advise of any destruction of records and include the date of and authority for such destruction.

I ask to be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: SOFNEX
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I request the records described below, created or received from July 1, 2017, through March 31, 2019.

Definition. In this request, "the Event" means a conference, symposium, or exhibition referred to as "SOFNEX" (including the variants "SOF NEX," "SOF-NEX," and "SOFNEX 2018"), focused on special operations forces and emerging technology, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, robotics and unmanned systems, big data, and intelligence analytics. Its organizers sought speakers and attendees from U.S. government agencies in 2017 and 2018. If the agency knows the Event under another name, please treat that name as an additional search term and tell me what it is.

Search terms. At a minimum, please search for: "SOFNEX"; "SOF NEX"; "SOF-NEX"; and the name of any organizer, venue, or alternate event title identified in the course of the search.

Records requested
1.	All emails (with attachments), calendar entries, and meeting invitations containing any of the search terms, including records concerning any invitation to GSA innovation staff (including Laura Gerhardt) to speak at or attend the Event, and any response.

Offices to search. The Technology Transformation Services (including 18F and the Centers of Excellence) and the Office of Government-wide Policy.

Instructions regarding search
•	Please follow any leads uncovered during the search, including referrals to other offices, record systems, or components, and conduct additional searches where those leads indicate responsive records may exist.
•	Please include records even if they are publicly available, and include all attachments to responsive emails.
•	"Records" includes emails and attachments, calendar entries and meeting invitations, memoranda, briefing papers, slide decks, letters, text and instant messages on government systems, approval forms, and handwritten notes. Please include drafts.
•	If any responsive records have been destroyed, please identify them and provide records relating to their destruction.
•	Please interpret the scope of this request broadly, short of an interpretation that would fail to reasonably describe the records sought.

Exemptions and segregability
Under the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016, 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A), GSA may withhold information only if it reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption, or if disclosure is prohibited by law. Please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of any record, identify the exemption claimed for each redaction, and release pages even if all that remains after redaction is letterhead, dates, or administrative markings. Please black out, rather than remove, redacted material. Where names of third parties are withheld under Exemption 6, I ask that titles, offices, and organizational affiliations be released.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti
